chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The entire forehead, from the middle of the hair of the head to the two eyebrows, is the place of prostration. So, whichever part from that falls to the ground, it suffices you, the measurement of a dirham and the measurement of the tip of the finger.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of the forehead that must touch the ground for prostration to be valid in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the precise anatomical boundaries for valid prostration, specifying the area from the hairline to the eyebrows as the primary site of sajdah. It establishes a jurisprudential flexibility by ruling that even minimal contact—equivalent to the size of a dirham coin or a fingertip—is sufficient to fulfill the obligation, reflecting the Shia emphasis on practical ease in ritual purity.
